examples.en: Seoul is currently the only special city in Korea.
There are really a lot of people in Seoul Special City.
Citizens directly elect the mayor of a special city.
The address on the envelope starts with Seoul Special City.

examples.ko: 일상에서는 특별시를 빼고 그냥 서울이라고 해요.
examples.en: In daily life we drop the special city part and just say Seoul.
Special cities and metropolitan cities are all big cities.

explain: '서울특별시'가 공식 이름이고, 일상에서는 그냥 '서울'이라고 해요. 부산·대구 같은 큰 도시는 '광역시'예요. 주소를 쓸 때는 '서울특별시 ○○구'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Seoul is a special city and Busan is a metropolitan city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국의 큰 도시 종류를 비교해 말할 때 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together to compare kinds of big cities in Korea.

phrases.en: My address is Mapo-gu, Seoul Special City.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주소를 공식적으로 쓸 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when writing an address formally.

explain_en: '서울특별시' is the official name, and in daily life people just say '서울'. Large cities like Busan and Daegu are '광역시' (metropolitan cities). In addresses, write it like '서울특별시 ○○구'.

examples.en: It is open only on certain days.

examples.ko: 이 약은 특정한 병에만 효과가 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine works only for a specific illness.

examples.ko: 특정하게 정해진 사람만 이 방에 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only specifically designated people can enter this room.
I do not use only one particular company's products.
It is a letter sent to no particular person.
The police pinned down the culprit and caught him right away.

explain: '특정'은 '어떤 정해진'이라는 느낌으로 명사 앞에 많이 붙어요. 보통 '특정한 사람', '특정 회사'처럼 말해요. 동사 '특정하다'는 범인을 특정하다처럼 수사 뉴스에서도 들려요.

phrases.en: I only use products from one particular company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특정' 뒤에 명사를 바로 붙이면 '어떤 정해진'이라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: '특정' directly before a noun means 'a certain, specific'.

phrases.example: 이 방은 특정한 사람만 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only certain people can use this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특정한'은 '특정'보다 조금 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '특정한' sounds a little softer than plain '특정'.

phrases.en: The police identified the culprit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 여러 가능성 중에서 하나를 정확히 정한다는 뜻이고, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb it means to pin down one among many; common in news.

explain_en: '특정' mostly attaches to a noun to mean a fixed, particular one, as in '특정한 사람' or '특정 회사'. The verb '특정하다' also appears in crime news, for example pinning down a suspect.

en: to correspond to; to be equivalent to; to be tantamount to

examples.en: This rule applies to every student.
It doesn't apply in my case.
Please mark the box that applies.
Children are eligible for this discount.
Only those it applies to should submit the form.

examples.ko: 이 조건에 해당될 때 연락 주세요.
examples.en: Please contact me if you meet this condition.

explain: 조건이나 규칙에 맞아서 적용된다는 뜻이에요. 서류에서 '해당 사항 없음'처럼 자주 보여요. '해당되는 것에 표시하세요'처럼 쓰고, 어떤 사람에게 적용되는지는 '에게'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Mark the place that applies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 설문에서 자주 보이는 꾸밈 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form often seen on forms and surveys.

phrases.en: It doesn't apply to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나와 상관없는 조건일 때 쓰는 고정된 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for a condition that doesn't concern you.

phrases.en: This age falls under the teenager category.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 범위나 종류에 속한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something falls within a certain range or category.

explain_en: It means a condition or rule fits a case and so applies. It appears often on forms in the phrase '해당 사항 없음' (not applicable). The person it applies to is marked with '에게'.

dis.h: apply to; passive form, used as predicate

p.n: Nearly identical; 해당하다 is also common as a modifier like 'the relevant'.

examples.en: Where to bury the nuclear waste is a big problem.
The news covered whether nuclear waste is stored safely.

examples.ko: 핵폐기물 처리 방법을 두고 의견이 갈려요.
examples.en: Opinions are split over how to handle nuclear waste.
I read an article about a nuclear waste storage site.
Nuclear waste can stay dangerous for a long time.
We had a discussion about nuclear waste in class.

explain: 뉴스나 사회·과학 수업에서 보는 말이에요. '처리하다', '보관하다', '매립하다' 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요. '핵폐기물 처리장'처럼 뒤에 장소를 나타내는 말을 붙이기도 해요.

phrases.en: I heard a nuclear waste disposal site is being built in our town.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처리장'을 붙여 핵폐기물을 처리하는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 처리장 names the place where it is processed.

phrases.en: Nuclear waste must be stored safely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 안전한 보관 문제를 이야기할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when talking about safe storage.

phrases.en: There is a method of burying nuclear waste underground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속에 묻어서 처리한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means disposing of it by burying it in the ground.

explain_en: This word appears in the news and in social studies or science classes. It often goes with verbs like '처리하다' (to process), '보관하다' (to store) and '매립하다' (to bury). A place word can follow it, as in '핵폐기물 처리장'.

en: to be exercised; to be used

examples.en: For a right to be exercised, certain conditions are needed.
The people's rights are being exercised properly.
The day the right to vote is exercised is coming.

examples.ko: 그 힘은 함부로 행사되면 안 돼요.
examples.en: That power must not be exercised carelessly.
The influence that was exerted was too big.
The authority couldn't be exercised, so the work was delayed.

explain: 주로 '권리·권한·영향력이 행사되다'처럼 법이나 제도 이야기에서만 써요. 소리가 같은 '행사(event)'와 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 능동형 '행사하다'(권리를 행사하다)가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: The police's authority is exercised according to the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리나 권한처럼 공식적인 힘이 쓰일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an official right or authority is put into effect.

phrases.en: The chairperson's influence was strongly exercised at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가의 힘이 결정에 작용했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that someone's influence had an effect on a decision.

phrases.en: That right has not yet been exercised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리를 쓰지 못한 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a right could not be used.

explain_en: Mostly used in law and institutions: '권리·권한·영향력이 행사되다'. It is different from '행사' (event). Rare in daily talk; the active '행사하다' (exercise a right) is more common.

examples.en: Under current law, it is hard to punish this behavior.

examples.ko: 현행법에 따르면 만 18세부터 투표할 수 있어요.
examples.en: According to current law, you can vote from age 18.

examples.ko: 현행법이 시대에 맞지 않는다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the current law doesn't fit the times.
The lawyer explained the current law in detail.
Under the current law, this kind of advertising is not allowed.

examples.ko: 현행법과 새 법안의 차이를 정리해 봤어요.
examples.en: I summarized the differences between the current law and the new bill.

explain: 지금 효력이 있는 법을 말해서 '개정안, 법안'과 비교할 때 자주 나와요. '현행법상 ~'은 뉴스와 법률 상담에서 흔한 표현이에요. 이미 없어진 법이나 앞으로 만들 법에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Under current law, this kind of act is illegal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 법률 상담에서 지금 법을 기준으로 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news and legal advice when speaking based on the law as it stands.

phrases.en: The National Assembly decided to amend the current law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 있는 법을 고쳐서 바꾼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means changing a law that already exists.

phrases.en: That contract goes against the current law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법을 어기고 있다는 사실을 조금 격식 있게 지적할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out, somewhat formally, that something violates the law.

explain_en: It refers to a law that is in effect now, so it often appears when compared with an amendment or a bill. '현행법상 ~' is a common phrase in news and legal consultations. It is not used for repealed laws or laws yet to be made.

examples.en: I live on the second floor of a multi-unit house.

examples.ko: 다세대 주택은 아파트보다 월세가 싼 편이에요.
examples.en: Rent in a multi-unit house tends to be cheaper than in an apartment.
There are many multi-unit buildings in this alley.

examples.ko: 다세대 주택으로 이사 가려고 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into moving to a multi-unit house.
Our home is a three-story multi-unit building.
Many multi-unit houses have narrow parking lots.

explain: 한 건물에 여러 가구가 따로 사는 작은 규모의 집을 말하며, 보통 '다세대 주택'으로 써요. 아파트보다 작고 '빌라'라고도 불러요. 부동산에서는 '다가구'와 구분해서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: My family lives in a multi-unit house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로 여러 가구가 사는 작은 건물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning a small building with several households.

phrases.en: I live in a small low-rise apartment building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '다세대 주택'을 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday word for '다세대 주택'.

phrases.example: 다세대 주택 월세가 아파트보다 싼 편이에요.
phrases.en: The monthly rent for a multi-unit house tends to be cheaper than for an apartment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 구하는 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about finding a home.

explain_en: It refers to a small building where several households live separately, usually '다세대 주택'. It is smaller than an apartment and is also called '빌라'. In real estate it is sometimes distinguished from '다가구'.

examples.en: They reclaimed part of the sea and built a new airport.
Land for burying garbage is running out.
The city decided not to fill in the tidal flats.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 예전에 호수를 매립한 곳이에요.
examples.en: This area is a place where a lake was filled in long ago.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 땅에 매립하면 냄새와 오염이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you bury garbage in the ground, smell and pollution can occur.

examples.ko: 항구 옆 바다를 매립했더니 땅값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: After the sea next to the port was filled in, land prices went up.

explain: 바다나 호수를 메워 땅을 만들 때와 쓰레기를 땅에 묻을 때, 두 가지로 써요. 그냥 '묻다'는 사람이나 물건 모두에 쓰지만 '매립하다'는 넓은 땅이나 쓰레기 같은 큰 규모에 써요. 명사 '매립지'도 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: The landfill is almost full.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매립한 땅이나 매립할 땅을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for land that is or will be filled in.

phrases.en: This land used to be sea but was reclaimed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매립하다'의 피동 표현으로 메워진 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on the result of being filled in.

phrases.en: They filled in the sea and made a large area of land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매립하다'의 쉬운 일상 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say '매립하다'.

explain_en: It is used in two ways: filling in sea or lake to make land, and burying garbage in the ground. Plain '묻다' (bury) works for many things, but '매립하다' is for large-scale cases like wide land or waste. Also learn the noun '매립지' (landfill site).

examples.en: This painting is not the original but a reproduction.
The museum is displaying only replicas.

examples.ko: 복제물을 팔 때는 표시를 해야 해요.
examples.en: When selling reproductions, you must label them.
Even though it's a replica, it was made as delicately as the real thing.
It isn't easy to tell a copy from the original.
This replica is smaller than the original.

explain: 그림, 유물, 문서처럼 원본을 똑같이 다시 만든 것이에요. 반대말은 '원본'이나 '진품'이에요. 일상에서는 '복사본'이라고 더 쉽게 말해요.

phrases.en: I left the original at home and brought only a copy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '복제물'보다 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday word than '복제물'.

phrases.en: It's hard to tell the replica from the original.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '원본'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with its opposite, '원본'.

phrases.en: The museum made a replica of the relic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원본을 똑같이 다시 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when recreating an original exactly.

explain_en: It refers to something made as an exact copy of an original, such as a painting, relic or document. The opposites are '원본' and '진품'. In daily speech people more simply say '복사본'.

en: attachment; being affiliated with a larger body

examples.en: This hospital is affiliated with the university.
The annex building has a library and a cafeteria.
I lost the accessory parts that came with the camera.
Many children attend the elementary school attached to the university.

examples.ko: 이 섬은 큰 섬에 부속된 작은 섬이에요.
examples.en: This island is a small one attached to the larger island.

examples.ko: 부속품은 상자 안에 따로 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The accessories are packed separately inside the box.

explain: '부속'은 큰 기관이나 물건에 딸려 있다는 뜻으로 '대학 부속 병원', '부속 건물'처럼 앞에 붙여 써요. 물건에 딸린 작은 부품은 '부속품'이라고 해요. '소속'은 사람이 어디에 속해 있는지 말할 때 써서 달라요.

phrases.en: I bought new parts for the washing machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 물건에 딸린 작은 부품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Small parts that come with a machine or object.

phrases.en: My father works at a university-affiliated hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 기관 안에 딸려 있는 병원을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a hospital attached to a larger institution.

phrases.example: 부속 시설에서 운동도 할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can also exercise at the attached facilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 건물이나 기관에 딸린 시설을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Facilities that belong to a larger building or institution.

explain_en: 부속 means attached to a larger institution or object and goes before the noun, as in 대학 부속 병원 and 부속 건물. The small pieces that come with an item are 부속품. 소속 is different: it describes which group a person belongs to.

t90.ax: This hospital is affiliated with the university.

examples.en: Please write the company's location on the form.
This building is located in Mapo-gu, Seoul.
Do you know where this school is located?
The head office's location changed, so I fixed the address.

examples.ko: 군청 소재지까지 버스로 한 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes an hour by bus to get to the county seat.

examples.ko: 소재지 확인이 안 되면 신청할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the location can't be verified, you can't apply.

explain: '소재지'는 건물이나 기관이 자리한 곳이에요. 사람이 사는 곳은 '거주지', 건물 주소는 '주소'라고 해요. 서류나 공문에서 많이 쓰고, '본사 소재지'처럼 기관과 함께 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 도시는 도청 소재지라서 관공서가 많아요.
phrases.en: This city is the provincial capital, so it has many government offices.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도청이 있는 도시를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used for the city where the provincial office is.

phrases.en: Please check the school's location in the document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 공문에서 위치를 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking a location in documents or notices.

phrases.en: The head office is located in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사의 본사가 있는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to where a company's head office is.

explain_en: 소재지 is the place where a building or an organization is located. Where a person lives is '거주지', and a building's address is '주소'. It is common in documents and official notices, together with an organization, as in '본사 소재지'.

dis.h: official place where an organization is situated
gh: general word for where something is
location judged by suitability for business

p.n: 위치 is the everyday word and can also mean exact position, not only the registered place.

t90.ax: Do you know where this school is located?

examples.en: Our company is located in Gangnam, Seoul.
That university is located in Busan.
I moved to the city where the head office is located.
The area where the factory is located is quiet.
Do you know where the post office is located?
The hospital is near the station, so it's convenient.

explain: 주소·위치를 공식적으로 말할 때 '~에 소재하다'로 써요. 말로는 '있다'나 '위치하다'가 더 자연스럽고, 서류·뉴스에서는 '소재지'(회사나 기관이 있는 곳)로 자주 봐요. 사람이 있는 곳에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Our school is located at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소재하다'보다 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More widely used than 소재하다.

phrases.en: Where is the company located?
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이나 회사가 있는 곳을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for where an institution or company is.

phrases.en: That hospital is near the city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to say it in daily conversation.

explain_en: Used officially for an address or location: '~에 소재하다'. In speech, '있다' or '위치하다' is more natural; in documents and news you often see '소재지' (where a company or office is located). It isn't used for where a person is.

gh: sit or stand in a place; descriptive

p.n: 자리하다 sounds more descriptive and less official.

t90.ax: That university is located in Busan.

examples.en: This company builds apartment complexes.
A professional did the bathroom work.

examples.ko: 다리를 시공하는 데 이 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took two years to build the bridge.

examples.ko: 바닥 타일을 직접 시공해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to try laying the floor tiles myself.
As soon as the design is done, we'll start construction.
A problem came up during construction and the work stopped.

explain: 시공하다는 설계도대로 건물이나 시설을 실제로 짓거나 설치하는 일이에요. 집수리나 인테리어에서 '시공 업체', '시공비'처럼 많이 들어요. 계획과 도면을 만드는 건 '설계'라고 하니 둘을 구분해서 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: I called the construction company for the house repairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사를 맡아 하는 회사를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the company that takes on a construction job.

phrases.en: I installed this floor myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '직접'을 붙여 전문가가 아닌 내가 스스로 공사했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '직접' you say you did the building work yourself.

phrases.en: We are constructing a new building now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 공사가 진행 중이라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-고 있다' you say the construction is in progress.

explain_en: 시공하다 means actually building or installing something according to the plans. You hear it in home renovation and interior work, as in '시공 업체' and '시공비'. Making the plans and drawings is called '설계', so keep the two apart.

en: inside of a building; inside of a house

examples.ko: 이 건물은 옥내 주차장이 있어서 비를 안 맞아요.
examples.en: This building has an indoor parking lot, so you don't get rained on.
Please take off your shoes inside the building.
The indoor swimming pool is crowded even in winter.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 행사를 옥내로 옮기기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to move the event indoors on rainy days.

examples.ko: 옥내 소화전 위치를 미리 확인해 두세요.
examples.en: Please check the location of the indoor fire hydrant in advance.

examples.ko: 옥내와 옥외 중에서 어디에서 결혼식을 할까요?
examples.en: Should we hold the wedding indoors or outdoors?

explain: 반대말은 '옥외'예요. 안내문이나 시설 설명에서 많이 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '실내'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Please take off your hat indoors.
phrases.nuance_ko: '옥내'와 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 옥내, but much more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: I parked my car in the indoor parking lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 안에 있는 주차장을 말하고 안내문에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a parking lot inside a building; often seen on signs.

phrases.en: You may not smoke inside the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 안내를 말할 때 조사 '에서는'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에서는 is typical when stating rules or notices.

explain_en: Its opposite is '옥외' (outdoors). You see it on notices and facility descriptions, while in everyday talk people usually say '실내'.

examples.en: The building extension work has started.
The school is noisy because of the addition.

examples.ko: 증축은 허가를 받아야 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only extend a building after getting a permit.
The house extension cost a lot of money.

examples.ko: 증축이 끝나면 교실이 두 개 늘어요.
examples.en: When the extension is done, there will be two more classrooms.
The hospital closed part of it for the extension.

explain: 있는 건물에 층이나 공간을 더 붙이는 건 '증축', 새로 짓는 건 '신축', 허물고 다시 짓는 건 '재건축'이에요. 공사 안내문과 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: The road is blocked because of the building extension work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사 안내문이나 뉴스에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in construction notices and news.

phrases.en: The hospital decided to build an extension.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물을 더 키우겠다는 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a plan to enlarge a building.

phrases.en: When will the building extension be finished?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것을 증축하는지 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put what is being extended in front of the word.

explain_en: Adding floors or space to an existing building is 증축, building a new one is 신축, and tearing down to rebuild is 재건축. You see these on construction notices and in the news.
